extra.message: EventRoutingService.matches() parses and evaluates a fully attacker-controlled 'expression' string with Spring's SpelExpressionParser against a StandardEvaluationContext, which permits type references and method invocation (e.g. T(java.lang.Runtime).getRuntime().exec(...)). The expression is sent verbatim from EventRoutingController.route() (POST /api/webhooks/route, reachable by any authenticated user per SecurityConfig's default authenticated() fallback). This allows arbitrary remote code execution via SpEL injection.

cwe: CWE-917: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an Expression Language Statement

extra.message: The path variable 'rule' from GET /api/reference/segments/{rule} is passed directly into Ognl.getValue(rule, vars). OGNL expressions can invoke arbitrary static methods and constructors (the same class of vulnerability behind Struts2 OGNL RCEs such as S2-045/S2-046), giving any authenticated caller a path to remote code execution.

cwe: CWE-917: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an Expression Language Statement

extra.message: request.reportUrl() from the POST /api/reports/render body is concatenated directly into a shell command string ('wkhtmltopdf ' + reportUrl + ' ' + outFile) and executed via 'cmd /c', with no validation or escaping. A value like "https://x" && calc.exe" or backticks/quotes lets an authenticated caller execute arbitrary OS commands on the server.

convertDocument() builds a shell command with the unvalidated 'format' parameter ('soffice --headless --convert-to ' + format + ' --outdir ' + outDir + ' ' + source) and runs it via 'sh -c'. 'format' comes straight from FileDownloadController's GET /files/documents/{id}/renditions?format= query parameter with no allow-list, enabling OS command injection by any authenticated user with access to the document.

importRenewalPolicy() loads an uploaded YAML document with 'new Yaml().load(document)'. The default SnakeYaml Constructor instantiates arbitrary Java types declared via YAML tags (e.g. '!!javax.script.ScriptEngineManager'), a well-known insecure-deserialization gadget chain leading to remote code execution from an uploaded file.

POST /partner/identity (permitAll, CSRF-exempt) parses the 'assertion' JWT with SignedJWT.parse()/getJWTClaimsSet() but never verifies its signature (no .verify(JWSVerifier) call). Anyone can craft an unsigned/self-signed JWT asserting any operator's email as the subject; the controller then changes that operator's identity's target user's role via userService.changeRole(), including promotion to PLATFORM_ADMIN. This is a full authentication bypass leading to privilege escalation.

cwe: CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature

extra.message: POST /partner/events (permitAll, CSRF-exempt) parses the 'assertion' JWT with JWTParser.parse()/getJWTClaimsSet() but never verifies the token's signature. Anyone can forge an assertion naming any enabled operator as the subject and thereby transition arbitrary deals and have the action attributed to that operator in the audit trail, with no proof the reseller actually issued it.

cwe: CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature

extra.message: searchByName() builds a SQL query by directly concatenating the 'name' parameter into the ILIKE clause ('... WHERE c.full_name ILIKE \'%' + name + '%\' ...') instead of using a JdbcTemplate parameter placeholder. 'name' comes unmodified from GET /api/reference/contact-search?name=, which only requires authentication, allowing SQL injection.

findAgents() builds an LDAP search filter by concatenating the unescaped 'team' value directly into '(&(objectClass=person)(department=' + team + '))'. 'team' is taken verbatim from the 'crm_directory_team' cookie in StaffDirectoryController, letting a client inject LDAP filter metacharacters (e.g. '*)(uid=*))(|(department=*') to broaden or bypass the intended search/filter logic.

cwe: CWE-90: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an LDAP Query

extra.message: readRenditionText() resolves the caller-supplied 'reference' directly under renditionRoot with Files.readString(renditionRoot.resolve(reference)) and performs no .normalize()/startsWith(baseDir) containment check (unlike openForDownload/store elsewhere in this same class, which do). 'reference' comes straight from the 'X-Rendition-Ref' request header in FileDownloadController.renditionText(), so a value like '../../../../etc/passwd' lets any authenticated user read arbitrary files on the server's filesystem.

archiveSourceFeed() resolves the user-supplied upload filename directly under archiveDir ('archiveDir.resolve(leaf).normalize()') and writes to it without checking the resolved path stays within archiveDir (no startsWith(archiveDir) guard, unlike DocumentService.store()). A crafted filename such as '../../../../some/other/path/file' lets staff overwrite arbitrary files reachable from the process's working directory.

archiveCustomerHealthReport() writes to 'new File(reportDropDir.toFile(), name)' where 'name' is taken unvalidated from ReportRenderController's POST /api/reports/archive?name= parameter, with no normalization or containment check against reportDropDir. A name like '../../../../etc/cron.d/x' allows arbitrary file write/overwrite on the server.

queueFor(user, scopeRef) looks up escalations by 'Long.valueOf(scopeRef.trim())' straight from the 'scope' query parameter (EscalationQueueView, GET /escalations?scope=) and returns them with no call to orgAccessService.assertAccess() and no role-based filtering (unlike the no-arg queueFor() it falls back to, which restricts SUPPORT_AGENT to their assigned escalations and CUSTOMER_CONTACT to their own organization). Any authenticated user — including a CUSTOMER_CONTACT or SUPPORT_AGENT for an unrelated account — can pass another organization's id in 'scope' and view its escalations.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: setContext()/summary() only call currentUserProvider.require() (authentication check) and never orgAccessService.assertAccess(). Any authenticated user (e.g. a CUSTOMER_CONTACT belonging to Organization A) can POST /api/portal/context with an arbitrary organizationId for Organization B, then GET /api/portal/context/summary to read Organization B's name, plan, and health score — bypassing the per-organization access control enforced everywhere else in the codebase via OrgAccessService.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: importFromLink() only checks the 'sourceUrl' scheme is http/https before calling restTemplate.getForEntity(sourceUrl, ...); there is no block-list/allow-list for internal/private network addresses (e.g. 169.254.169.254, localhost, internal service hostnames). A staff user can make the server fetch and store the response of any internal endpoint reachable from it, enabling SSRF against internal infrastructure.

The CORS configuration for '/api/**' allows any origin ('allowedOriginPatterns("*")') together with 'allowCredentials(true)'. This lets any website embed the CRM's authenticated session and call its JSON APIs cross-origin with the victim's cookies, enabling CSRF-like data theft/actions across all /api/** endpoints.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: http.headers(hdrs -> hdrs.frameOptions(fo -> fo.disable())) disables the X-Frame-Options protection application-wide (every Vaadin view, login, admin screens — not just the intended partner status-widget route), making the entire authenticated application embeddable in a hidden iframe on an attacker page and exposing it to clickjacking attacks.

cwe: CWE-1021: Improper Restriction of Rendered UI Layers or Frames

extra.message: On a SecurityException, the download endpoint redirects to the value of the incoming Referer header (response.sendRedirect(returnTarget)) without validating it is an internal/relative path. A crafted link that causes the victim's browser to send an attacker-controlled Referer (or a forged request) results in the server issuing a redirect to an arbitrary external URL.

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')
